title: openai-compat: Responses API seed/determinism + metadata passthrough, streaming & tool-calling compatibility
author: Alyssa Chen
description: Add compatibility mappings and runtime handling for newer OpenAI Responses API semantics: seed/determinism flags, metadata passthrough on responses, structured output stability, and improved streaming/tool-calling fallbacks. Motivation: customers relying on OpenAI-compatible SDKs expect consistent behavior when switching to Redwood's runtime, including deterministic outputs for seeded requests and preservation of response metadata for audit/observability. This PR implements: 1) request-level 'seed' and 'deterministic' translation into our deterministic sampling layer and KV-cache keying; 2) passthrough of response.metadata -> openai.responses[*].metadata for both sync and streaming modes; 3) structured output tokenization fixes to reduce malformed JSON in streaming; 4) tool/function-calling compatibility shim (map 'tool' call events to our internal 'action' events and back); 5) e2e backwards-compatible tests and new unit tests in openai_compat/; 6) migration note for clients relying on old OpenAI-compatible 'choices' shape. Checklist: - [x] Compatibility mapping for seed/deterministic flags - [x] Preserve response.metadata in sync + streaming - [x] Structured output streaming stabilization - [x] Tool/function calling shim + event mapping - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] CI green (after fix) Related: Linear ENG-3314, ENG-3489. See design notes: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3314/openai-responses-semantics
